skmr now keeps writable skills in one personal library, with global and project placements sharing the same content.

## What's new

- Automatically adopt unambiguous writable skills when opening a scope. Duplicate names wait for an explicit choice; built-in and plugin skills remain view-only.
- Use `skmr add` for library skills, local paths, GitHub URLs, skills.sh pages, and packs. Add to the current project or pass `--global` to enable everywhere.
- Import local authoring folders as owned copies while preserving the source.
- Manage project placements, remote search and updates, and group presets directly in the TUI.
- Use one durable operation journal for content, placements, and links, including recovery across interrupted multi-scope changes.
- Permanently delete unused library skills after removing global, project, and group dependencies.
- Get started with a much shorter README.

## Changes for existing users

- Replace `skmr import <url>` with `skmr add <url> --global` or `skmr add <url>` in a project. Remote project adds store content centrally without enabling it globally.
- The `move` and `copy` commands are replaced by placements: `skmr add <skill> --project <path>` and `skmr remove <skill> --project <path>`.
- Inventory and the TUI open in the nearest Git project by default. Use `--global` or `--project <path>` to select a scope; projects outside Git require `--project`.
- Opening an older project migrates its owned skill library to personal storage and repairs discovery links. Name conflicts and replaced links stop migration for review.
- Groups are fixed presets. Adding `@group` saves its current members as direct skill requests; later group changes do not update the project. Remove installed members by skill name rather than `@group`. Existing group requests preserve their last resolved members during migration.
- `skmr restore` returns adopted content to its origin and excludes it from automatic adoption until explicitly added again. Imported skills have no adopted origin; remove their placements and use `skmr delete` instead.
- Dry runs and diagnostics do not automatically adopt or upgrade skills. Open an older scope with `skmr list` before previewing changes.
- Recover interrupted operations with `skmr doctor --recover`, or `skmr doctor --recover --project <path>`. Historical journals remain recoverable.

## Install or upgrade

```sh
brew update
brew upgrade faizmokh/tap/skmr
```

Or install with Go 1.25+:

```sh
go install github.com/faizmokh/skmr/cmd/skmr@v0.5.0
```
